name: Indian Bank
business_summary: Chennai-based public sector bank (founded 1907; merged Allahabad Bank in 2020), 73.84% government-owned. Deposits and advances of roughly Rs10 lakh cr and Rs8 lakh cr (derived), strong in south India with retail/agri/MSME focus. Q2 FY27: net profit Rs3,462cr (+15%, headline; screener Rs3,541cr), NII +18%, and a Rs1,388cr gain on sale of NSE shares was disclosed on 2026-10-16 (whether fully in Q2 profit is unverified). Mcap Rs1.2 lakh cr, P/E 9.1, P/B 1.38, ROE 15.4%, dividend yield 2.1%.

exposures.mechanism: +3pp system loan growth: PSU banks have been growing 10-14% (UCO guides 12-14%); NII +3% -> PAT +4% x 0.5 => +2. Higher-beta than ICICI because PSU deposit growth lags, but operating leverage is also higher.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 profit +15% (Rs3,462cr), NII +18%, shares fell 3% then recovered (CNBC TV18/Business Standard/NiftyTrader)

exposures.mechanism: +3pp deposit growth: PSU CASA ~38-40% (model knowledge); CoF -5bp -> NIM +3bp -> PAT +2-3% x 0.5 => +1.5. Deposit growth is the binding constraint for PSU banks, so a modest positive.

+25bp: ~60% of loans are EBLR/repo-linked (PSU banks highest in sector, model knowledge) on ~Rs8 lakh cr loans (derived) => asset yield +15bp; deposits reprice with ~3-6 month lag on ~50% => CoF +8bp => NIM +7bp = +2.5% NII, PBT +4%, PAT +4% x 0.25 = +1.0; less valuation/credit-demand -0.7 => +0.3. Hike on 2026-10-07 favours PSU banks relative to ICICI (-0.5).

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo to 5.50%, stance calibrated tightening (Hindu/Reuters/Moneycontrol headlines)

exposures.mechanism: +25bp: investment book ~Rs2.5 lakh cr (derived, ~28% of assets) with AFS/HFT ~40% at duration ~2.5 => MTM ~Rs600cr pre-tax = ~3.5% of annual PBT (~Rs17k cr) x 0.5 persistence (recovers as bonds roll to par) => -1.0; discount-rate effect at 1.38x P/B => -0.8; total -1.8.

evidence.note: screener: Sep-2026 qtr net profit Rs3,541cr (headlines Rs3,462cr), TTM Rs13,220cr, mcap Rs1,20,176cr, P/E 9.1, P/B 1.38, ROE 15.4%, govt 73.84%

exposures.mechanism: +50bp credit cost: loans ~Rs8 lakh cr x 0.5% = Rs4,000cr vs annual PBT ~Rs17.5k cr => PAT -23%; persistence 0.5, EV/MCap 1.0 => -11; PSU PCR is high (>90% on NPAs, model knowledge) and recoveries are strong so the effective hit is lower => -8.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 profit +15% (Rs3,462cr), NII +18%, shares fell 3% then recovered (CNBC TV18/Business Standard/NiftyTrader)

exposures.mechanism: Unsecured retail is <8% of the PSU book (model knowledge): +1pp delinquencies x 8% x 60% = 5bp = Rs400cr = 2.3% of PBT x 0.5 => -1.2, rounded -1.0.

exposures.mechanism: Tightening step (provisioning on project finance, ECL framework from FY28 per RBI plans, model knowledge): PSU banks with ROE 15% and CET1 ~14% have room, but ECL provisioning transitions weigh on payout: -1.5.

evidence.note: screener: Sep-2026 qtr net profit Rs3,541cr (headlines Rs3,462cr), TTM Rs13,220cr, mcap Rs1,20,176cr, P/E 9.1, P/B 1.38, ROE 15.4%, govt 73.84%
